stories.headline: MediaTek launches Dimensity CX C10 Max, a 3nm laptop SoC for Google's new Googlebooks

key_facts.fact: MediaTek launched the Dimensity CX C10 Max on September 21, 2026, the same day Googlebooks went on sale, as the first SoC in its new Dimensity CX laptop line
key_facts.excerpt: MediaTek is launching the CPU on the same day Googlebooks go on sale (September 21), and the company says it will power an upcoming Googlebook device.

key_facts.fact: The chip is built on TSMC's 3nm N3 node with eight CPU cores (one Cortex-X925, three Cortex-X4, four Cortex-A720), an 11-core Immortalis-G925 GPU and MediaTek's NPU 890 rated at up to 55 TOPS
key_facts.excerpt: It's built on a 3nm node (TSMC N3) and uses an all-performance-core design, packing eight cores on the CPU and 11 cores on the GPU, along with MediaTek's NPU 890, delivering up to 55 TOPS of AI performance

key_facts.fact: Specs are nearly identical to MediaTek's previous Kompanio Ultra 910 flagship — same GPU, NPU, 12MB L3 and 10MB system cache — with the main upgrade being LPDDR5X memory speed rising from 8,533MT/s to 9,600MT/s
key_facts.excerpt: The biggest difference, at least based on the specs MediaTek has shared, is memory speed. Both use LPDDR5X, but the C10 Max climbs up to 9,600MT/s from 8,533MT/s on the Kompanio Ultra 910.

key_facts.fact: MediaTek claims up to 15% faster multi-threaded performance and 50% lower single-threaded power than Qualcomm's Snapdragon X Elite X1E-84-100, but ran the comparison on different platforms (ChromeOS reference board vs. a Windows 11 Galaxy Book 4 Edge) and published no absolute numbers
key_facts.excerpt: It claims the C10 Max has up to 15% faster multi-threaded performance and 50% lower power in single-threaded workloads ... the test platforms were completely different, with MediaTek using a reference board running ChromeOS R133 for its chip and using a Galaxybook 4 Edge with Windows 11 from Samsung for Qualcomm's chip.

key_facts.fact: Googlebooks, announced September 21, are a new Android-based laptop category from Acer, ASUS, Dell, HP and Lenovo starting at $899, with Intel Core Ultra Panther Lake and Qualcomm Snapdragon X options alongside MediaTek
key_facts.excerpt: Google unveils Googlebook hardware, with flagship devices from Acer, ASUS, Dell, HP, and Lenovo, offering deep Android integration, coming in October for $899+

sources.title: MediaTek's next-gen Dimensity CX C10 Max will power new Googlebook initiative alongside Intel and Qualcomm

stories.headline: Nscale files for NYSE IPO: $103.4B in contracts, but only $2.6B active and 85% from two clients

key_facts.fact: Nscale Global Holdings filed its S-1 with the SEC on September 18, 2026 to list on the NYSE under ticker NSCL, seeking up to $3 billion, with Goldman Sachs, J.P. Morgan and Morgan Stanley leading 23 underwriters
key_facts.excerpt: Nscale Global Holdings Ltd. today filed to go public on the New York Stock Exchange. ... Last month, sources told Bloomberg that Nscale is seeking up to $3 billion. The company was valued at $14.6 billion in March.

key_facts.fact: The filing shows $103.4 billion in active and contracted total contract value as of August 31, up from $38 billion at the end of 2025, but only $2.6 billion — about 2.5% — was classified as active
key_facts.excerpt: Only $2.6 billion, or about 2.5%, of the $103.4 billion total was classified as active at August 31. Nscale had approximately 25,000 active graphics processing units against 461,000 active and contracted GPUs.

key_facts.fact: Microsoft agreements provide for payments of up to $43.8 billion through December 2033 and Anthropic agreements signed in August for up to $44.6 billion — together roughly 85% of the contract book
key_facts.excerpt: Microsoft agreements provide for payments of up to $43.8 billion through December 2033, while Anthropic agreements signed in August provide for up to $44.6 billion. Together, those amounts are equivalent to roughly 85% of the disclosed contract total.

key_facts.fact: Nscale posted $140.6 million of revenue in the first half of 2026 against a net loss of $1.02 billion, and had not obtained binding financing commitments for the equipment and infrastructure required by the Anthropic contracts
key_facts.excerpt: $103.4 billion in signed customer contracts, $140.6 million in first-half revenue and $27.5 billion of equipment and construction commitments ... including a $44.6 billion agreement with Anthropic for which Nscale had not secured binding financing commitments when it filed.

key_facts.fact: A September 15 financing agreement covers at least $3.1 billion — $2.1 billion of convertible notes plus a $1 billion Nvidia investment expected to close around November 16
key_facts.excerpt: A September 15 financing agreement covers at least $3.1 billion, comprising $2.1 billion of convertible notes and a further $1 billion Nvidia investment through notes or nonvoting shares.

key_facts.fact: Bloomberg reported the disclosure represents a 1,000-fold increase in contracts over three years, driven by Microsoft and Anthropic, and that Nscale has not yet secured financing for the Anthropic deal
key_facts.excerpt: Nscale's 1,000-fold increase in contacts over the last three years is mainly due to two clients thirsty for artificial intelligence computing capacity: Microsoft Corp. and Anthropic PBC. Those companies make up 85% of the $103 billion in total contract value ... Nscale hasn't secured financing for the Anthropic deal yet.

stories.headline: Local opposition blocked or delayed 45 US data centers worth $68B in Q2, Data Center Watch says

key_facts.fact: Data Center Watch's new report found 45 US data center projects worth about $68 billion were blocked or delayed by local opposition between April and June 2026
key_facts.excerpt: Data center opposition blocked or delayed 45 US projects worth $68 billion between April and June, according to research group Data Center Watch.

key_facts.fact: Those 45 projects accounted for more than half of all new large-scale data center developments the firm tracked in the quarter
key_facts.excerpt: A new report from Data Center Watch indicates that these 45 affected projects account for more than half of all new large-scale data center projects the firm began tracking in the second quarter.

key_facts.fact: The Q2 figure is down from the record first quarter, when 75 projects worth roughly $130 billion were blocked or delayed — meaning at least 120 projects were disrupted in the first half of 2026
key_facts.excerpt: In the first quarter of this year alone, 75 U.S. data center projects were blocked or delayed, involving roughly $130 billion in investment. This means that in the first half of this year, at least 120 projects have had their original development schedules impacted by local opposition.

key_facts.fact: Data Center Watch counts 843 anti-data-center groups active across 49 states — every state except Hawaii — and says around 30 statehouses have introduced or adopted measures on siting, electricity and water use
key_facts.excerpt: Data Center Watch reports that there are currently 843 organizations opposing data center construction across 49 U.S. states, with Hawaii being the only exception.

key_facts.fact: Chief analyst Miquel Vila said new local groups keep forming, opposition is spreading to more states and jurisdictions, and online petition signatures keep climbing
key_facts.excerpt: Miquel Vila, the agency's chief analyst, stated that new local organizations continue to emerge, opposition activities are spreading to more states and local jurisdictions, and the number of signatures on online petitions is steadily increasing.

key_facts.fact: Bloomberg reported the study on September 21, noting opposition to data centers continues to mount in the US
key_facts.excerpt: Data Center Watch: 45 US data center projects valued at $68B were blocked or delayed by local opposition from April to June, or 50%+ of large Q2 developments

stories.headline: First industry-wide count: only ~7,000 humanoid robots were sold worldwide in 2025, IFR data show

key_facts.fact: Around 7,000 humanoid robots were sold worldwide in 2025 for industrial and professional service use, according to International Federation of Robotics figures reviewed by Reuters and reported on September 21
key_facts.excerpt: AMSTERDAM, Sept 21 (Reuters) - Around 7,000 humanoid robots were sold worldwide last year for industrial and professional service use, figures compiled by the International Federation of Robotics showed.

key_facts.fact: That compares with roughly 542,000 conventional industrial robots installed in 2024 and an estimated 199,000 professional service robots sold that year
key_facts.excerpt: This compares with around 542,000 regular industrial robots installed in 2024 and another estimated 199,000 service robots sold that year for use in transport, hospitality and cleaning.

key_facts.fact: IFR secretary general Susanne Bieller said humanoids remain 'a fraction' of the global robot population; the federation has compiled robotics statistics for three decades but is collecting humanoid data for the first time
key_facts.excerpt: However, the numbers of humanoids remain "a fraction" of the overall robot population globally, Susanne Bieller, secretary general of Frankfurt-based IFR, said. ... IFR has compiled robotics statistics for three decades, and has begun collecting humanoid data alongside its much larger industrial robot and service robot figures for the first time.

key_facts.fact: Many of the humanoids sold in 2025 never did productive work — they went to research institutions or to companies using them to generate training data for AI models
key_facts.excerpt: Many humanoid robots sold last year never did a day of productive work. They went to research institutions, or to companies that used them to generate data for training AI models.

key_facts.fact: Bank of America Global Research estimates 90,000 humanoid robots will ship in 2026 and 1.2 million by 2030; IFR's tally excludes consumer and military humanoids, with medical robots classified separately
key_facts.excerpt: Bank of America Global Research estimates that 90,000 humanoid robots will be shipped in 2026 and 1.2 million by 2030. The IFR's tally is based on supplier and national industry association data, and excludes consumer and military humanoid robots, while medical robots are classified separately.

key_facts.fact: IFR's definition requires a human-like appearance and autonomous operation in human environments, though legs are not required; full 2025 industrial and service robot data will be published September 24
key_facts.excerpt: Its definition requires a human-like appearance and autonomous operation in environments designed for people, although a robot does not necessarily need legs to qualify.

stories.headline: China's regulator slows humanoid-robot IPOs, questioning state-backed revenue and valuations

key_facts.fact: Chinese regulators are using informal 'window guidance' to hold back humanoid-robot listings, with one person saying humanoid IPOs have effectively been frozen for now and another describing it as a sector-specific slowdown rather than a formal ban
key_facts.excerpt: Regulators have used informal "window guidance" to hold back some humanoid-robot listings, said the people ... One of them said humanoid IPOs had effectively been frozen for now, while another said there was no formal ban, describing the move as a sector-specific slowdown.

key_facts.fact: The slowdown was mainly triggered by Unitree Robotics' volatile debut: the stock soared more than fivefold in Shanghai a month ago and has since slumped 55% from its peak
key_facts.excerpt: The slowdown was mainly triggered by a volatile start for shares in Unitree Robotics, a maker of humanoid and quadruped robots, they said. The stock soared more than fivefold in its Shanghai debut a month ago and has slumped 55 per cent from its peak.

key_facts.fact: At least half a dozen Chinese humanoid firms are preparing to list, including Deep Robotics, X Square Robot and AGIBOT
key_facts.excerpt: At least half a dozen Chinese humanoid robotics firms are preparing to go public, including Deep Robotics, X Square Robot and AGIBOT.

key_facts.fact: Regulators are scrutinizing revenue from local-government-backed projects such as robot data-collection centres and joint ventures where governments provide 80%-90% of initial investment; one person estimated some robot companies' valuations could fall 60%-70% if that revenue were stripped out
key_facts.excerpt: The person said robot data-collection centres, where robots are trained, and joint ventures, in which local governments could provide 80 per cent to 90 per cent of initial investment, had generated significant revenue for some companies. ... The person estimated that valuations at some robot companies could fall 60 per cent to 70 per cent if revenue associated with data-collection centres were stripped away.

key_facts.fact: Qianchuang Capital's Leo Wang called the robotics investment wave 'campaign-style innovation', said hype around embodied AI exceeded China's internet and new-energy booms, and noted some private-market projects had already taken valuation cuts of 30%-50%
key_facts.excerpt: Leo Wang, a venture capitalist at Qianchuang Capital, described the investment wave in the robotics sector as "campaign-style innovation" ... Some private-market projects had already suffered valuation cuts of 30 per cent to 50 per cent.

key_facts.fact: Mainland Chinese companies have raised $148.9 billion through share sales and convertible offerings so far in 2026, up 59% year-on-year, with technology companies accounting for 41% of the total
key_facts.excerpt: They have raised US$148.9 billion (S$189.9 billion) through share sales and convertible offerings so far in 2026, up 59 per cent from the same period a year earlier, according to LSEG data. Technology companies raised 41 per cent of the total.

sources.title: China slows humanoid robot IPO rush as hype outruns reality

stories.headline: Samsung says HBM4 yields hit ~80%, shifting from catching up to flooding the market with volume

key_facts.fact: Industry sources said on September 20 that yields on Samsung's sixth-generation HBM4 have climbed to around 80% — the level the industry calls a 'golden yield' — after falling below 60% early in mass production
key_facts.excerpt: According to industry sources on the 20th, yields on Samsung's HBM4 fell below 60% in the early stages of mass production but have recently climbed to around 80%.

key_facts.fact: Samsung projects third-quarter HBM4 revenue will more than triple quarter-on-quarter and expects HBM4 to be more than 60% of total HBM revenue in the second half; related revenue passed $1 billion three months after mass-production shipments began in February
key_facts.excerpt: The company projected that third-quarter HBM4 revenue would more than triple from the previous quarter. It also expects HBM4 to account for more than 60% of total HBM revenue in the second half. Three months after announcing the start of HBM4 mass-production shipments in February, related revenue surpassed $1 billion

key_facts.fact: Samsung's HBM capacity, measured in average monthly wafer input, is projected to rise nearly 40% from about 180,000 wafers this year to about 250,000 next year, which may further squeeze commodity server and PC DRAM supply
key_facts.excerpt: Samsung's HBM production capacity, measured by average monthly wafer input, is projected to rise nearly 40% from about 180,000 wafers this year to about 250,000 next year. ... As more wafers are allocated to HBM production, supply of commodity DRAM used in servers and PCs may be constrained.

key_facts.fact: HBM4 sells for about 2 million won per chip, more than double the price of fifth-generation HBM3E
key_facts.excerpt: HBM4 is known to sell for about 2 million won per chip, more than double the price of HBM3E, the fifth generation.

key_facts.fact: Counterpoint Research data show Samsung's HBM revenue share jumped to 33% in Q2 from 21% in Q1 while SK hynix slipped to 50% from 58%, narrowing the gap from 37 points to 17
key_facts.excerpt: According to Counterpoint Research, Samsung's HBM market share by revenue jumped to 33% in the second quarter from 21% in the first quarter. Over the same period, SK hynix slipped to 50% from 58%. The gap between the two narrowed to 17 percentage points in the second quarter from 37 percentage points in the first.

key_facts.fact: Goldman Sachs raised its Samsung target to 490,000 won and added the stock to its Conviction Buy list in a September 18 report, after management said 2027 memory supply-demand would be tighter than 2026 and that new capacity would go mainly to DRAM and HBM
key_facts.excerpt: Following an online meeting with Samsung Electronics' management, Goldman Sachs reaffirmed its Buy rating and included the stock on its Conviction Buy list in a report issued on September 18, 2026. The target price for common shares is KRW 490,000 ... management expects the supply-demand ratio in 2027 to be tighter than in 2026.

stories.headline: DeepSeek bets on Huawei training chips, with first deliveries expected in Q4 2026 or Q1 2027

key_facts.fact: DeepSeek CEO Liang Wenfeng told investors that training on Huawei chips is one of the company's biggest bets, with Huawei set to deliver training chips in Q4 2026 or Q1 2027, The Information reported on September 21
key_facts.excerpt: Sources: DeepSeek CEO Liang Wenfeng says training on Huawei chips is one of DeepSeek's biggest bets and Huawei is set to deliver training chips in Q4 or Q1 2027 — DeepSeek CEO Liang Wenfeng told investors that a major priority for his company is to use more domestic chips to train its models

key_facts.fact: Liang said the company wants to use more Chinese-made training chips and hopes to receive a new batch of Huawei chips in Q4 2026 or Q1 2027, according to two people familiar with the matter
key_facts.excerpt: DeepSeek CEO Liang Wenfeng told investors that the company wants to use more Chinese-made training chips and added that it hopes to receive a new batch of Huawei's chips in the fourth quarter of 2026 or the first quarter of 2027.

key_facts.fact: The chip at the centre of the transition is Huawei's Ascend 950DT; DeepSeek is weighing a deployment of at least 160,000 of them at a roughly 1-gigawatt data centre in Ulanqab, Inner Mongolia
key_facts.excerpt: The chip at the center of this transition is Huawei's Ascend 950DT, a processor that has reportedly shown stable results in testing. DeepSeek is reportedly contemplating a deployment of at least 160,000 of these chips at a new data center in Ulanqab, Inner Mongolia, with the facility expected to draw roughly 1 gigawatt of power.

key_facts.fact: DeepSeek completed full-parameter post-training of its V4 Pro model on about 1,000 Ascend 910C chips in June 2026, and Huawei has pulled forward its next-generation Ascend 960DT training chip to Q1 2027 — roughly three quarters early — on high demand from Chinese AI developers
key_facts.excerpt: DeepSeek already completed full-parameter post-training of its V4 Pro model using around 1,000 Ascend 910C chips back in June 2026. ... Huawei has pulled forward the launch of its next-generation Ascend 960DT training chip to Q1 2027, roughly three quarters ahead of the original schedule, due to unusually high demand from Chinese AI developers.

key_facts.fact: DeepSeek is training a 2-trillion-parameter model with an 8-trillion-parameter model also planned, and the CEO told investors that moving training to domestic chips 'has to work'
key_facts.excerpt: @hesamation: DeepSeek is training a 2T model, with an 8T model also planned ... ALSO they expect new Huawei training chips in Q4 2026 or Q1 2027 apparently the CEO told investors that moving to train on domestic chips "has to work."
